articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Bayern's Karl to get 'dream' Real Madrid move?
articles.description: Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl could get his dream move to Real Madrid, while AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are keeping tabs on Bayern Munich attacking midfielder Lennart Karl, according to Bild's Christian Falk. Los Blancos are among several teams interested in the 18-year-old, with whom the Bundesliga champions plan to open contract renewal talks, while rival clubs monitor whether Michael Olise's presence in his position could create a transfer opportunity. Karl said during an event in January that playing for Madrid would be a "dream" which led to an apology after the comments sparked anger among Bayern fans.

- AC Milan are planning to sign USMNT winger Christian Pulisic to a new contract extending until the summer of 2031, according to Corriere dello Sport. Initial talks have begun with the 28-year-old's representatives over a deal worth around €5 million per season following his goal-scoring performance in Sunday's 3-0 win over Lecce.

- Chelsea are considering Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton and Feyenoord's Gjivai Zechiël as potential successors to Enzo Fernández, TEAMtalk reports. The 22-year-old Zechiel has registered five goals and four assists in seven Eredivisie matches this season, attracting interest from Chelsea, Liverpool, and five other Premier League clubs.

- Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri is being scouted by Juventus, according to Gazzetta dello Sport. The 25-year-old tops the Bianconeri shortlist for the January transfer window, with a loan approach lined up due to his lack of playing time under Enzo Maresca, while RB Leipzig's David Raum is considered an alternative.

- Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa are interested in Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-Jae, according to Christian Falk. Both clubs have tracked the 29-year-old South Korea international since the summer, though any move is expected to depend on upcoming contract discussions with the German club.

Other rumors

- Arsenal are among four Premier League teams tracking Sturm Graz midfielder Luca Weinhandl, 17. (TEAMtalk)

- Barcelona sent scouts to watch Athletico Paranaense defender Arthur Dias in their 2-1 victory over Bahia on Sunday. (Sport)

- Bayern Munich are not considering a move for Newcastle United striker Nick Woltemade, who is currently on loan at Juventus, despite recent reports. (Christian Falk)

- Liverpool, Arsenal, and Chelsea are among the clubs tracking Real Sociedad defender Jon Martín. (Ekrem Konur)

- Aston Villa are preparing contract extension talks with attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía. (Daily Mail)

- Roma and AC Milan are lining up a loan approach for Real Madrid striker Endrick in January. (Calciomercato)

articles.headline: Orioles sweep doubleheader against Blue Jays to stave off elimination -- for now
articles.description: — Trey Gibson pitched brilliantly into the seventh inning and the Baltimore Orioles beat the Toronto Blue Jays 4-2 on Wednesday night to sweep a doubleheader and at least temporarily stay alive in the American League playoff race.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — Trey Gibson pitched brilliantly into the seventh inning and the Baltimore Orioles beat the Toronto Blue Jays 4-2 on Wednesday night to sweep a doubleheader and at least temporarily stay alive in the American League playoff race.


              One more loss by the Orioles — or a win by the Chicago White Sox, who lost 5-4 at Kansas City on Wednesday night — would eliminate Baltimore. The Orioles also won the opener 4-2 against Toronto, then the 24-year-old Gibson (2-3) was outstanding in the nightcap.


              He would have completed at least seven innings if not for a rare defensive positioning violation that kept the top of the seventh going. Sean Keys grounded out to second for the third out, players left the field, and the Orioles were already playing “Thank God I'm a Country Boy” — which comes after "Take Me Out to the Ball Game" during the seventh-inning stretch — when an umpire interrupted the song to say the Blue Jays were challenging.


              A replay appeared to show second baseman Jeremiah Jackson's heel on the outfield grass before the grounder, so Keys was awarded first. The play was scored an error on Jackson, but no at-bat was charged to Keys. Gibson walked the next hitter and was pulled. Yennier Cano then issued a walk before striking out Myles Straw with the bases loaded to end the inning for real.


              In his eighth career start, Gibson allowed three hits in 6 2/3 scoreless innings with seven strikeouts and two walks. Christian Encarnacion-Strand homered and drove in three runs.


              Davis Schneider hit a two-run homer for Toronto in the ninth. The Blue Jays, eliminated from the playoff chase with their loss in the first game, are assured a losing season one year after winning the AL pennant.


              Toronto starter CJ Van Eyk (0-2) allowed four runs and four hits in five innings.


              Encarnacion-Strand opened the scoring with a two-run single in the first, then scored on Colton Cowser's double. Encarnacion-Strand's solo shot in the fourth made it 4-0.


              Two of the three hits Gibson allowed were infield singles in the third.


              Up next
              Both teams are off Thursday. The Orioles play the Yankees in New York on Friday night, and the Blue Jays host Cincinnati.


              ------

articles.headline: Alonso hits 41st homer as Orioles beat Blue Jays 4-2 to eliminate Toronto from the playoff race
articles.description: — Pete Alonso hit his 41st home run of the season, Chris Bassitt took a shutout into the sixth inning and the Baltimore Orioles beat the Toronto Blue Jays 4-2 in the first game of a doubleheader Wednesday, eliminating the defending American League...
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — Pete Alonso hit his 41st home run of the season, Chris Bassitt took a shutout into the sixth inning and the Baltimore Orioles beat the Toronto Blue Jays 4-2 in the first game of a doubleheader Wednesday, eliminating the defending American League champions from the postseason race.


              The Orioles and Blue Jays both entered this twin bill one loss from elimination. The best the Blue Jays (77-81) can do now is finish .500 — a season after they pushed the Los Angeles Dodgers to extra innings in Game 7 of the World Series.


              Max Scherzer (3-9) allowed four runs and four hits in five innings in the 500th appearance — and 491st start — of his career. He struck out seven and walked three. With his future uncertain, the 42-year-old right-hander could come back on short rest to pitch again Sunday in the season finale.


              The 37-year-old Bassitt (9-5) allowed two runs and seven hits in five-plus innings. He was pulled with two on in the sixth and both runners scored on second baseman Jeremiah Jackson's throwing error.


              Andrew Kittredge pitched the ninth for his 11th save.


              Scherzer struck out three in the first, but Jackson hit an RBI single in the second for the Orioles. With men on first and third and two out, Jackson took off for second, then stopped and got in a rundown. Colton Cowser was slow leaving third, but the Blue Jays kept going after Jackson, allowing Cowser to score.


              Alonso's two-run shot in the fifth pulled him even for the AL lead in homers with Houston's Yordan Alvarez and Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero. Alonso is eight RBI ahead of Alvarez for the league lead and may be the man who spoils the Houston slugger's pursuit of a Triple Crown.


              Up next
              Neither team had announced a starter for the second game Wednesday night.


              ------

articles.headline: Is Sullivan the next Olise? Comparisons for USMNT's top young stars
articles.description: With the USMNT welcoming a new class of debutantes during this international break, ESPN dives into the numbers of the United States' next prodigies.
articles.body:
If one word defines the first call-up for the U.S. men's national team since the summer's FIFA World Cup, it's this: youth.

To give the next generation some opportunities, coach Mauricio Pochettino has given several key figures a break and instead selected a noticeably younger group for upcoming friendlies in late September and early October.

Of the 28 chosen, 13 have yet to make their senior national team debut. From those 13, eight are teenagers who are continuing to fine-tune and develop their talents.

Though some of these players are literally still kids, they also represent an exciting generation of up-and-comers who have the potential to become elite game changers for the U.S. by the time the 2030 World Cup rolls around, if not sooner.

Shining a light on a few of these fresh faces, we've selected five names to follow in the upcoming international break. We've also enlisted the help of ESPN's in-house guru Bill Connelly, who has provided key stats (over the last 365 days in all competitions) on each name, as well as both overly optimistic and realistic comparisons to players that they could one day become.

Zavier Gozo | Midfielder | 19 | Crystal Palace

Within just three years, Gozo went from earning his MLS debut in 2023 with Real Salt Lake to then gaining a high-profile move to the Premier League this summer with Crystal Palace.

Typically playing on the right flank, the 19-year-old midfielder has an immense amount of energy with 8.1 progressive carries per 90 minutes. In fact, even though Gozo hasn't played in MLS since July -- before his move to the Premier League -- he still ranks second overall in MLS for total progressive carries, carries following a defensive action, and take-ons, among teenagers in MLS.

"He is insanely robust. If I were to tell you the running numbers he's putting up, they're, for his age, I think world-class," said Nate Miller, a former assistant at Real Salt Lake, to ESPN.

With six goals and five assists across 1,614 minutes in the last year, the attack-minded midfielder has stepped up with his 3.1 shots per 90 minutes. He is also crucial in regaining the ball thanks to his 6.8 defensive interventions per 90 minutes. Looking back at teenagers within MLS, Gozo is still second in 2026 when it comes to total tackles.

"We don't know who's going to come through," said Miller about the next generation of U.S. stars. "But he should be one of the main guys in the national team in the future."

When Albert stepped onto the pitch in April for German side Borussia Dortmund, the midfielder made history as the youngest American to play in the Bundesliga at the age of 16. articles.headline: Longtime Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter dies
articles.description: Lawrence Tanter had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days until his retirement in June following a stroke.
articles.body:
Longtime Los Angeles Lakers public-address announcer Lawrence Tanter has died, the team announced Wednesday.

"We are deeply saddened to share the news of the passing of legendary Lakers public address announcer Lawrence Tanter," the team wrote in a statement shared on its social media accounts. "For 43 years, LT's voice served as the soundtrack to Lakers games at the arena. He will be remembered as a cherished member of the Lakers family."

In June, the 76-year-old Tanter retired from his courtside post where he had manned the microphone in L.A. since the "Showtime" days of the 1980s.

Tanter had suffered a stroke late in the regular season and missed the Lakers' last six home games, plus the playoffs.

Last month, shortly before entering into hospice care, Tanter texted ESPN.

"Quote me," he wrote, "'It's been a blessing.'"

Known by Lakers fans simply by his initials, LT, Tanter was the longest-tenured PA announcer in team history and was recognized for his style as much as for his longevity.

Despite being equipped with a booming baritone voice and an imposing 6-foot-7 frame, Tanter's presentation relied on restraint, using a silky-smooth delivery to share the Lakers' starting lineups, substitutions, fouls and score announcements with an aim to inform rather than distract the audience.

Tanter channeled his parallel career as a disc jockey at various jazz radio stations in L.A. when he reported to the arena, often wearing an eight-panel cap atop his head and sporting a well-manicured white goatee on his chin.

Always part of the tapestry but never stealing the spotlight, Tanter's signature call became announcing "The Laker girlllssss" when the dance team finished a routine and scampered off the court.

Tanter's role was particularly poignant during the Lakers' most recent championship season in 2019-20. When the Lakers played their first game after Kobe Bryant's death in January 2020, Tanter introduced all five Lakers starters with the same line: "6-6, 20th year out of Lower Merion High School, Kob-eeeeee Bryant!" Later that season, when the Lakers competed in the NBA bubble in Orlando, Florida, and eventually won the championship, Tanter recorded player introductions at a home studio in the Porter Ranch area of Los Angeles that were played before Lakers games at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex.

The Chicago native played forward for his high school basketball team and received a scholarship to attend the University of Dubuque in Iowa.

He went on to be a part of 10 Lakers championships and 16 Western Conference titles.

"Lawrence Tanter has been an integral part of the Lakers gameday experience for more than four decades, setting the tone for countless memorable moments with his professionalism, energy and signature booming voice," Lakers acting governor Jeanie Buss said in June when Tanter was shifting to an advisory role. articles.headline: Harrison Jr. blocking out noise amid slow start for Cardinals
articles.description: Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. hears and reads what's being said about him after his slow start to his third season, but he remains confident and still has the confidence of his teammates.

Harrison, who has one catch for 33 yards on four targets through two games, said Wednesday that he's not surprised by the reaction to his slow start, but said it hasn't been difficult to keep his confidence high. He didn't hesitate when asked where the level of it is, saying he has "a lot of confidence in myself."

"Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn't going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So, I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from.

"And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything."

Quarterback Jacoby Brissett said Wednesday that "nobody has lost confidence in Marv" despite his start, while Harrison didn't shy away from the reality, citing a number of reasons.

"It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really.

"So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general."

Another reason, Harrison said, is because of the two defenses he's played this season. The Los Angeles Chargers gave him single coverage on just seven of 32 routes and the Seattle Seahawks are, simply, one of the best defenses in the NFL.

"Pretty much that simple," Harrison said. "Seattle's a really good defense and you don't want to give a lot of teams, especially a rival team, a lot of credit. But when you just look across the league, they're far beyond above everybody else, especially on the defensive side of the football. So, things like that happen."

Brissett said the two have had "good conversations" and has tried to lend an ear to Harrison whenever he needs it.

"It's easy to say, 'Oh, it's a long season' to other people, but to Marv it doesn't feel like it's a long season," Brissett said. "As a teammate and as a quarterback, you still have to be there for him because what if this week goes the same way? Am I just going to not be there?
